The ld. counsel for the plaintiff has submitted that the plaintiff has proved its case on the basis of the ex parte evidence led.
It is submitted that there is no defence by the defendants and the pleadings as well as evidence of the plaintiff is unrebutted and uncontroverted.
It is submitted that as such the plaintiff would be entitled to decree in terms of the prayer clauses of the plaint.
It is further submitted that the defendants have deliberately avoided the proceedings and have also prevented the seizure of the goods by the local commissioner.
It is submitted that the defendants are dealing in counterfeiting and unfair trade practices.
It is submitted that the defendants cannot be permitted to take advantage of their own wrong and that the case calls for punitive damages.

Reliance is placed on LT Foods Ltd. v. Saraswati Trading Co. 2022/DHC/004806.

sentences.text: The persons at the said premises did not permit the local commissioner to inspect the premises or make inventory of the goods in the premises as per the orders of the Court.

Thus, it appears that the defendants have adopted the strategy of avoiding and staying away from the proceedings of the present case and have also prevented the inspection of the premises and goods by the local commissioner.
There is no reason why the defendants would not appear in the present suit if they had any defence to the suit.
I would hold that on a balance of probabilities on the basis of the ex parte evidence led, the plaintiff has proved its case as pleaded in the plaint.
The plaintiff would be entitled to decree of permanent injunction as prayed for in the plaint.
The defendants have not rendered any accounts.
The defendants also did not permit the local commissioner to inspect the premises and goods.
The defendants have adopted the strategy of avoiding the proceedings.
